skin.setting: a Venetian palazzo during the winter carnival, 1897
skin.title: Carnival of the Drowned
skin.place: Palazzo Gradenigo on the Grand Canal, Venice
skin.styleGuide: Rich oil painting aesthetics, chiaroscuro candlelight, damp marble reflections, gilded stucco, deep velvets, and wintry Venetian canal mist.

rooms.name: the canal terrace
rooms.description: An outdoor marble terrace lining the Grand Canal, chilled by winter winds and lap of brackish water.

rooms.name: the masking vestibule
rooms.description: An arched entry hall lined with gilded mirrors and pegs for feathered carnival cloaks.

rooms.name: the music salon
rooms.description: A lavish chamber with a harpsichord, velvet settees, and frescoed ceilings of Apollo and the muses.

rooms.name: the grand portego
rooms.description: The central hall of the palazzo, flanked by gothic pointed arches and tall lancet windows.

rooms.name: the private study
rooms.description: A secluded walnut-paneled sanctuary filled with ledgers, glass cabinets, and antique maps.

rooms.name: the ballroom
rooms.description: A cavernous hall of polychrome marble and Murano chandeliers where the senator's body was discovered.

people.name: Count Alvise Moro
people.bio: A proud Venetian nobleman whose family prestige has dwindled while his debts have mounted. He attended the gala ostensibly to discuss an ancestral art sale.
people.voice: Haughty and defensive, speaking with aristocratic disdain.
people.motive: The senator held promissory notes that threatened to bankrupt the Moro family estate completely.
people.portrait: A severe man in his late fifties with slicked iron-grey hair, a sharp aquiline nose, thin lips, and a tall, rigid frame dressed in a tailored midnight-blue evening suit with velvet lapels.

people.name: Signora Bianca Foscolo
people.bio: A celebrated soprano from La Fenice who was hired to entertain the evening's masquerade guests. Her glittering career masks a turbulent past entangled with the senator.
people.voice: Melodramatic and breathless, carrying the cadence of the stage.
people.motive: The senator possessed private correspondence that could ruin her reputation and end her stage career.
people.portrait: A poised woman in her thirties with voluminous raven hair swept into an elaborate chignon, dark expressive eyes, high cheekbones, and an emerald silk gown adorned with black lace trim.

people.name: Dr. Carlo Renier
people.bio: A discreet physician who has tended to the city's elite behind closed doors for decades. His professional facade hides a deep resentment of the senator's exploitative nature.
people.motive: The senator was blackmailing him regarding a fatal medical malpractice incident from years ago.
people.portrait: A gaunt man in his forties with neatly trimmed brown beard, wire-rimmed spectacles over tired grey eyes, slightly stooped posture, wearing a formal black frock coat and high collar.

people.name: Elena Balbi
people.bio: A sharp-witted young heiress who lived under her uncle's overbearing control. She was determined to secure her financial independence before he could arrange her marriage.
people.motive: She stood to inherit the entire Gradenigo estate and escape a forced marriage to an aging merchant.
people.portrait: A slender young woman with honey-blonde hair gathered under a pearl-embroidered snood, piercing hazel eyes, a resolute chin, wearing a heavy crimson velvet dress with slashed sleeves.

people.name: Matteo Ziani
people.bio: An ambitious antiquarian and dealer who arranged transactions between impoverished nobles and foreign buyers. His business dealings with the host had recently turned hostile.
people.motive: The senator discovered he had forged several provenance documents and threatened to report him to the authorities.
people.portrait: A broad-shouldered man in his late thirties with dark wavy hair, an oiled mustache, a watchful gaze, wearing a dark charcoal wool coat over an embroidered brocade waistcoat.

people.name: Senator Giorgio Gradenigo
people.bio: A ruthless merchant senator who hosted the masked carnival ball at his ancestral palazzo. His murder ended a lifetime of merciless manipulation and accumulated wealth.
people.portrait: An imposing, heavy-set man in his sixties with a silver goatee, florid complexion, wearing an opulent damask doublet with gold thread embroidery and ruffled cuffs.

skin.briefing: On the misty night of Carnival in 1897, the masked revelry at Palazzo Gradenigo came to a sudden halt when Senator Giorgio Gradenigo was found dead on the cold marble floor of the ballroom. The heavy doors and labyrinthine salons kept the guests confined within the grand residence as fog rolled across the Grand Canal. Five individuals who bore deep grievances against the senator were present during the fateful hours. As the investigating magistrate, you must sift through their testimonies, house records, and physical traces to establish everyone's whereabouts and identify who ended the senator's life.
skin.scene: A dim Venetian ballroom viewed through an arched doorway, illuminated by flickering chandeliers, with damp marble floors reflecting cold light, masked figures in carnival cloaks murmuring in the shadows.
skin.summingUp:
Look at how the candlelight gutters against the damp marble, casting long, bruised shadows across the gilded stucco and heavy velvets. The canal mist presses thick against the windows, yet the truth in this palazzo is stark and unyielding. We begin with Card 3, which narrows down when the murder happened, proving at once that the murder was not at seven in the evening or midnight.

From there, the spatial geometry of this crime closes in. We know that the killer and Senator Giorgio Gradenigo were both in the ballroom when it happened. Because of this undeniable fact, Signora Bianca Foscolo is in the clear.

Following that exact same reality—that the killer and Senator Giorgio Gradenigo were both in the ballroom when it happened—Count Alvise Moro and Elena Balbi are in the clear, and the murder was not at nine in the evening, ten in the evening, or eleven in the evening. By this very same presence in the ballroom, Dr. Carlo Renier is likewise in the clear.

Only a single hour and a single figure remain amidst the gloom. The hour was eight in the evening, and the killer is Matteo Ziani, who struck down Senator Giorgio Gradenigo in the ballroom after the senator uncovered his forged provenance documents and threatened to deliver him to the authorities.
